title: SBA E-Tran API Integration: A Practical Guide for Lenders and Fintech Teams
summary: Build SBA E-Tran integrations on ELend, not deprecated ETran. Learn credentials, TEST setup, XSD validation, and error handling.
body_markdown:
SBA E-Tran API integration lets lenders move SBA loan applications from their own systems into SBA without rekeying data. This guide covers the ELend web services, credentials, testing, validation, and the platform layers that feed E-Tran.


‍


### What Is SBA E-Tran API Integration?


SBA E-Tran API integration connects a lender's loan origination system (LOS) or lending platform to the SBA's ELend web services. It lets lenders submit and service SBA loan applications system-to-system instead of through E-Tran web screens. ELend is the current web-service interface, and ETran is the legacy one.


Volume makes automation worth the build. In its[SBA FY2025 lending announcement](https://www.sba.gov/article/2025/09/30/trump-sba-delivers-record-capital-small-businesses-fy25) , the U.S. Small Business Administration said it guaranteed about 77,600 7(a) loans totaling about $37 billion in FY25.


In this setup, the LOS is the system of record that submits through E-Tran. Lendflow's[SBA lending software guide](https://www.lendflow.com/post/sba-lending-software-how-to-choose-a-platform-that-speeds-decisions-without-adding-headcount) covers how to choose that platform.


Program rules come from[SBA SOP 50 10](https://www.sba.gov/document/sop-50-10-lender-development-company-loan-programs) , the U.S. Small Business Administration's procedure for lender loan programs. Version 8.1 took effect Oct 1, 2026, and its text refers to "E-Tran Servicing, or successor SBA Loan System."


Treat E-Tran as the final step in the stack. Data, decisioning, and execution layers feed it—so submission quality depends on everything upstream.


‍


### ELend vs. Legacy ETran: Build on ELend


Skip the legacy interface—build every new integration on ELend. The U.S. Small Business Administration's[SBA ELend API documentation](https://catran.sba.gov/apidocs/elend.cfm) states that "ETran still exists for existing clients, but is now deprecated for new web service client development."


ELend was derived from ETran, and both run the same backend code through different entry paths. ELend's structure-in/structure-out design has not required WSDL changes to add services. SBA's vendor FAQ adds that Etran.wsdl and its methods are no longer supported for new work.


Attribute ELend Legacy ETran


Status Current web-service interface Legacy interface


Existing clients Supported Still exists for existing clients


Backend code Same code as ETran Same code as ELend


Design Structure-in/structure-out: one Inputs, one Outputs Separate methods defined in Etran.wsdl


WSDL Elend.wsdl Etran.wsdl, no longer supported for new work


New builds Recommended Deprecated for new clients


The lesson applies beyond SBA. Stable, API-first contracts age better than monolithic interfaces, a theme Lendflow explores in[API-first vs. traditional LOS](https://www.lendflow.com/post/lendflow-vs-traditional-loan-origination-systems-2025-comparison-for-brokers) .


‍


### How the ELend Request and Response Model Works


Every ELend call in an SBA E-Tran API integration uses one input structure and one output structure. That single pattern covers origination and servicing, so teams build one request flow and reuse it across services.


#### The Inputs structure


The Inputs structure is a set of name/value pairs that SBA calls "keys." The MethodNamePhysical key tells ELend which service to run. The remaining keys supply that service's parameters.


- **PasswordUpdate:** Pairs MethodNamePhysical with a NewPassword key to change the user's password.
- **ExtractOrigination:** Pairs MethodNamePhysical with an ExtractOptions key to request an origination extract.
- **Credential keys:** CLSUsername and CLSPassword ride along on every call, as covered below.


#### The Outputs structure


Every response returns the same Outputs structure. Four keys drive most client logic.


Key What it carries How to use it


ErrorMessageEnglish Plain-language error text Surface to loan operations staff


ErrorMessageTechnical Technical error detail Log for developers and SBA support


PasswordUpdateRequired Flag that the password must change Trigger the password rotation workflow


ResponseData Service payload in XML or JSON Parse and write back to the LOS


#### WSDL and XSD schemas


Point your client at the[SBA ELend WSDL file](https://caweb.sba.gov/elend/ws/elend.wsdl) , published by the U.S. Small Business Administration. It defines the endpoint` https://caweb.sba.gov/elend/ws/elend.cfc` .


As of November 2026, SBA's ELend page lists version 9.3 as the latest origination and servicing XSD, with "curr" aliases for the current version. Shared types live in SBA_SimpleTypes.xsd and SBA_ETranTypes.xsd. A separate XSD defines the OriginateStatus response.


Pin to versioned XSDs—then track SBA releases and upgrade on your schedule. A "curr" alias moves when SBA publishes a new version.


‍


### Authentication and Credentials


Every ELend service requires two keys: CLSUsername and CLSPassword. They identify a CapAccess Login System (CLS) account.


Vendors connect using the lender (partner) CAFS user ID and password. The same account serves both screen access and API calls.


The U.S. Small Business Administration's[SBA vendor API FAQ](https://catweb2.sba.gov/apidocs/vendrFaq.cfm) is explicit: "SBA does not provide non-expiring system to system credentials to lenders." SBA web services use individual user credentials only, and PasswordUpdateRequired means you need a rotation plan.


Treat the credential lifecycle as a workflow with owners and alerts. Build these three controls in from day one.


- **Ownership:** Assign a named user for the integration and document who can rotate the password.
- **Rotation:** Check every response for PasswordUpdateRequired and route it to that owner right away.
- **Storage:** Keep credentials in a secrets manager and out of application code.


‍


### Test Environment and Vendor Onboarding


Every SBA E-Tran API integration tests on its own credentials. Per SBA's vendor FAQ, production credentials do not work in TEST automatically, so request both account sets at the start.


Production and test accounts typically take 1–3 business days to provision, per the same FAQ. Partner (lender) and vendor setup differ, so confirm which path applies before filing requests. Lenders request the "Enter/Edit your SBA Loan Applications" role under ETRAN for the correct Location ID.


Step Owner Action


1 Lender Confirm the CAFS/CLS user account the integration will use


2 Lender Request the "Enter/Edit your SBA Loan Applications" role under ETRAN for the Location ID


3 Lender or vendor Request separate TEST credentials


4 Operations Plan for a typical 1–3 business days of provisioning


5 Developer Load Elend.wsdl and pin the 9.3 XSDs


6 Developer Validate XML against the XSD before each submission


7 Developer Build PasswordUpdateRequired handling into the client


SBA access is one timeline, and your front-end build is another. Lendflow's guide to[fintech infrastructure for lending](https://www.lendflow.com/post/fintech-infrastructure) puts widget launches at under two weeks and full API integrations at 30–45 days.


‍


### Error Handling and Validation


Catch data errors upstream—before they hit your SBA E-Tran API integration. The U.S. Small Business Administration's vendor API FAQ (linked above) draws a clear line between errors and warnings.


- **Errors:** Resolve every error message before submission.
- **Warnings:** Ignore them if needed, since SBA says they do not impact application submission.
- **Optional fields:** Leave non-mandatory fields blank when you have no data.
- **Location ID:** Send the correct Location ID for the lender.
- **Schema checks:** Validate XML against the XSD before every call.
- **Success signal:** Read a null ErrorMessage as a successful call.
- **Support tickets:** Send SBA all output keys when reporting an error.


SBA's backend also checks that the borrower has no application with another lender. Give your operations team a clear path for handling that result.


‍


### Loan Numbers and Servicing Data


Per SBA's vendor FAQ, the SBA loan number is generated instantaneously after the application backend validations are completed. Write it back to the LOS as soon as ELend returns it.


Post-origination data runs through a separate service. The U.S. Small Business Administration's[SBA LoanList v3 documentation](https://catweb.sba.gov/apidocs/loanlist.cfm) says users can "request and process up to 1,000 loans in a single API call."


LoanList v3 is an FTA Portal loan data service, separate from E-Tran origination. It returns LoanHeader, LoanPayment, LoanPaymentOriginator, LoanPaymentLender, and Balance data over REST or SOAP.


‍

### FAQs


#### How does ELend differ from the legacy ETran component?


ELend runs the same backend code as ETran but uses a more flexible structure-in/structure-out design. SBA says ETran is deprecated for new web service client development.


#### What credentials does the E-Tran API require?


Every ELend service requires CLSUsername and CLSPassword, using the lender's CAFS account.


#### Do production credentials work in the E-Tran test environment?


No. The TEST environment requires separate credentials.


#### How long does it take to get E-Tran test and production accounts?


Per SBA's vendor FAQ, it typically takes 1–3 business days.


#### Do validation warnings need to be cleared before submission?


No, warnings do not impact submission. Error messages must be resolved first.


#### How long does it take to get an SBA loan number?


SBA generates the loan number instantaneously after backend validations are completed.


#### Can new integrations use the Etran.wsdl endpoint?


No. Elend.wsdl replaces that endpoint, and SBA no longer supports Etran.wsdl methods.
